title: How to Choose a Document Digitization Company: 12 Questions to Ask Before You Sign
summary: Choosing a document digitization company? Ask these 12 questions on image quality, accuracy, security, capacity, pricing, and exit terms before you sign.
body_markdown:
Choosing the wrong document digitization company rarely looks like a mistake on signing day. It shows up months later as missing pages, blurred scans, files indexed under the wrong names, slipped deadlines and rescans billed as extras. For regulated records, it can also leave a compliance gap that surfaces in the next audit.


A document digitization company converts paper, film and mixed media records into searchable digital files, then indexes them and delivers them into the systems your teams already use. Providers of[document digitization services](https://xbpglobal.com/solutions/document-digitization/) tend to look alike on a shortlist, so the real difference is what each one will commit to in writing.


This guide covers the 12 questions to ask before you sign, grouped into four decision areas, along with how to prepare and how to turn the answers into a choice.


## What to Define Before You Talk to Any Vendor


You prepare for a document digitization project by defining your volume, document mix, quality needs, compliance rules and timeline before you contact a single vendor, because without those facts you cannot tell a strong answer from a polished one. Experienced providers, XBP Global among them, will ask for the same facts in the first call.


- **Volume.** Roughly how many boxes, pages or images, and whether new paper keeps arriving after the backfile is done.
- **Document mix.** Standard paper, bound books, oversized drawings, photographs, film or fragile originals, and the rough share of each.
- **Quality and data needs.** The resolution you need, which fields must be indexed and how accurate they must be.
- **Compliance rules.** Which regulations apply, and whether originals must be kept, returned or destroyed.
- **Timeline and systems.** Your deadline and the system the files must land in, such as your document management platform.


Put these in a one page brief and send the same brief to every vendor, so their answers are comparable from the start.


## How to Choose a Document Digitization Company on Image Quality and Accuracy


You choose a document digitization company on image quality and accuracy by asking which standard it scans to, how it measures accuracy and what it does when a batch fails. Providers with more than 30 years in document processing answer all three in numbers, which is the bar every vendor on your shortlist should meet.


### 1. What image standard will you scan to?


A named resolution in dots per inch, a color mode for each document type and a recognized standard behind both. NARA rules for federal records set a minimum equal to the FADGI category for modern textual records, which makes a useful benchmark even outside government\[1\]\[3\] .


**What to request:** Sample images of your own documents at the stated settings, plus the written scan specification the vendor will follow.


### 2. How do you measure and report OCR and indexing accuracy?


An accuracy figure that states whether it is measured per character, per field or per document, reported to you every week. Field accuracy matters most, because one wrong account number breaks retrieval. Leading production scanners report character recognition accuracy as high as 99.99%.


**What to request:** A recent accuracy report from a live project, along with the method behind it and how human review checks machine extraction.


**Example:** A national records office held about 108.2 million birth, marriage and death records dating back to 1837, with around 91.3 million still on paper. Varied record types, cursive handwriting and deteriorating media made digitization complex, and paper records slowed certificate production. XBP Global demonstrated its[AI powered IDP solution](https://xbpglobal.com/case-studies/streamlining-record-digitisation-for-the-general-register-office/) through a proof of concept that combined secure record tracking, scanning and automated transcription, with human review for anything automation could not resolve. The solution automates data extraction, validates information and flags issues with suggested fixes, removing the manual bottlenecks in certificate production.


### 3. What does your quality control check, and what happens to a failed batch?


Checks on every image during capture, a sampling plan after it and a rescan rule for any batch that fails. Live image quality monitoring and double feed detection catch blurred, skewed or stuck pages before they leave the scanner, which costs far less than finding them months later.


**What to request:** The written quality control procedure, the failure rate that triggers a full batch rescan and confirmation of who pays for it.


## Security and Compliance Questions to Ask a Document Scanning Vendor


The security questions to ask a document scanning vendor cover where your documents travel, which audits cover the work and whose hands touch them. Providers already running SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant mail operations for health insurers answer these with documents, and any vendor who cannot should slow your decision.


### 4. How is the chain of custody tracked from pickup to return or destruction?


A logged chain of custody that records every handoff, from pickup and transport through scanning, storage and return or certified destruction. Each box and batch should be tied by barcode to a timestamped audit trail. NARA rules on when source records may be destroyed after digitization offer a useful benchmark\[2\] .


**What to request:** A sample custody log from a past project showing where one specific file was on a given day.


**Example:** A telecommunications enterprise ran its mail from a headquarters spanning more than 100 floors, half of them set up for agile and remote workers, which caused delivery delays and poor visibility. Its bankruptcy and subpoena teams also needed chain of custody tracking for sensitive legal documents. XBP Global, already supporting the client with 145 mailroom, concierge and courier staff, ran a digital mailroom pilot that tracked every item through its lifecycle and gave employees same day digital access through a secure portal. The pilot saved more than six hours a day across key departments and gave the legal teams full[chain of custody visibility](https://xbpglobal.com/case-studies/digital-mailroom-for-a-leading-telecommunications-enterprise/) .


### 5. Which certifications cover the site that will handle our documents?


Named attestations covering the specific site and team doing your work, such as a current SOC 2 Type II report, plus a signed business associate agreement wherever health information is involved. A company level certificate means little if the scanning happens somewhere else.


**What to request:** The current report with its date and scope, checked against the facility named in your contract.


### 6. Who touches our documents, and is any work subcontracted?


Trained staff employed by the vendor, working in facilities it operates, with background checks, role based access and any subcontractor named in the contract. Unnamed partners create custody gaps you cannot audit.


**What to request:** A written map of where each stage happens, onshore or offshore, and a clause that stops that location changing without your approval.


## Can a Document Scanning Company Handle Your Volume, Formats and Systems?


A document scanning company can handle your volume, formats and systems when it commits capacity in writing, scans mixed media within one program and delivers files your systems accept from day one. A provider whose platform reads documents in more than 120 languages shows how wide that coverage can reach.


### 7. What daily capacity is committed to our project?


A committed daily volume backed by named equipment and staff, with a surge plan for backlogs. Production scanners that capture 240 documents a minute and hold over 1,000 pages per load make high daily targets realistic.


**What to request:** The capacity commitment in writing, plus the plan for your timeline when another client project peaks.


### 8. Can you scan mixed formats in the same project?


Yes, with past examples covering bound volumes, oversized drawings, photographs and film alongside standard paper. Splitting formats across vendors multiplies handoffs and custody risk.


**What to request:** Samples from a past mixed format project that match the formats in your brief.


### 9. How will files be named, indexed and delivered into our systems?


A file naming and indexing scheme agreed in writing before scanning, delivered in formats and metadata your document management system accepts without rework. The NARA validation checklist is a good test, since it requires every record in scope to be digitized and all metadata to be accurate, complete and correctly labeled\[1\] .


**What to request:** A sample delivery folder from a past project and a test load into your own system.


## Pricing and Contract Questions for a Document Digitization Vendor


Pricing and contract questions for a document digitization vendor decide what the project really costs and how easily you can leave. A provider that delivered $10 million in annual savings for one healthcare insurer can talk about value in hard figures, so expect the same precision on every term in the contract.


### 10. How is pricing structured, and what costs extra?


An itemized price per unit, with preparation, indexing, rescans, transport, storage and return or destruction listed separately. Most surprises come from document prep and from indexing fields added after the quote.


**What to request:** The vendor definition of a billable page, since one double sided sheet can count as two images, plus a fixed price for a pilot batch.


### 11. What does the SLA cover, and what is the remedy for errors and delays?


A service level agreement that sets turnaround, accuracy and rescan times for each batch, with credits or remedies when the vendor misses them. Deadlines without remedies are only intentions.


**What to request:** The draft SLA, the progress reporting format and the plan for clearing a backlog.


**Example:** A law firm with three US offices struggled to keep work moving when stay at home orders sent its staff remote, and it needed[a new mail system within days](https://xbpglobal.com/wp-content/uploads/info-sheets-case-studies/digital-mailroom-for-disaster-recovery-for-law-firm-infosheet.pdf) , with chain of custody tracking and full information security. XBP Global presented a solution within 48 hours, set up a dedicated PO box and routed the mail to a nearby processing center for digitization. Within 10 days of signing the statement of work, the mail for the firm was being received, processed and distributed digitally, with capacity for 100% of its volume.


### 12. Who owns the images and data, and how do we exit?


Confirmation that you own every image, index and piece of metadata, that your data stays in the region you specify and that a full export comes back in open formats if you leave.


**What to request:** Written exit terms covering handover time, cost and certified destruction of copies left on vendor systems. Exit terms are easiest to agree before signing, while you still hold every option.


## How to Compare Document Digitization Companies


You compare document digitization companies by scoring every vendor on the same scale and weighting the areas that matter most to your project. Providers such as XBP Global expect this kind of written comparison, because it rewards answers backed by evidence.


1. **Score each answer.** Give 2 points for a strong answer with proof, 1 for a partial answer and 0 for a vague or missing one.
2. **Weight what matters to you.** Use your one page brief. A regulated archive might double the security scores, while a large backfile might double capacity.
3. **Treat red flags as deal breakers.** A vendor that cannot show a custody log, a current attestation or written exit terms should not stay on the list, whatever its total.
4. **Shortlist two or three.** Take the highest weighted scores forward to a pilot.


## How to Test a Document Digitization Company Before You Sign


You test a document digitization company with a paid pilot batch built from your hardest documents and scored against acceptance criteria you set before scanning starts. Providers trusted by more than 60 Fortune 100 companies expect this step, because a pilot shows real output on your own documents within weeks.


Choose a few hundred pages that represent your worst cases, such as faded carbons, mixed sizes, staples, sticky notes and handwriting. Agree the image standard, accuracy target and indexing fields in writing first, then run the same sample through every finalist. Compare the pilot output with what each vendor promised in writing, and the right partner usually becomes clear.


## How XBP Global Answers These 12 Questions


XBP Global supports more than 2,000 clients with approximately 9,000 professionals across 20 countries, and its document digitization work answers each of the four decision areas with evidence you can check.


- **Image quality and accuracy.** Production scanners capture images at 600 dpi, with Triple Read accuracy at capture. The Xtractr engine then extracts and validates data fields at 99.9% accuracy, sends only uncertain fields to human reviewers and uses every correction to retrain the model.
- **Security and compliance.** Every document and every extraction carries a full audit trail. Personal data is identified and redacted at the point of extraction, and GDPR and HIPAA tracking runs across every document.
- **Volume, formats and systems.** The service handles invoices, contracts, medical records, legal filings, engineering drawings and fragile historical records, including documents too delicate for standard equipment. Validated data goes straight into SAP, Oracle, Salesforce or another system of record, so nothing is keyed in again by hand.
- **Testing before you commit.** Every engagement starts with a discovery call and a proof of concept on your own documents, with no IT effort needed from your side. Live deployment typically follows within two weeks of contract, and larger backfile projects are scoped by volume.
